key_insight: Cryorolled commercially pure titanium develops a ~50 nm grain structure that coarsens during annealing and fully recrystallizes at 945 K.
engineering_relevance: Temperature-dependent relaxation informs heat-treatment choices for retaining nanostructure or promoting recrystallization in cryorolled titanium.
method: Cryogenic rolling at 100 K to a true strain of 1.20.
Electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction to characterize structural evolution.
evidence_signal: X-ray diffraction showed slight crystallite growth at 525 K, accelerated coarsening at 725 K, and complete recrystallization at 945 K; reported growth kinetics gave an exponent of ~4 and activation energy of ~97 kJ/mol.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify annealing durations or kinetic-fit uncertainties, limiting direct translation into processing schedules.
paper_title: Thermal Stability and Structural Relaxation Kinetics of Commercially Pure Titanium
